svg.title: Module 05 one-page guide: LLMs as Reasoning Engines & Tools as Contracts
svg.text: CSCI 391 · MODULE 05 · ONE-PAGE LECTURE GUIDE
LLMs as Reasoning Engines & Tools as Contracts
The model proposes; the tool contract decides what actually happens.
Part II · Core Capabilities · Week 5 · Read: Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 5–6
OPENING CASE
One added sentence in a tool description — stating what the tool does not do — eliminated an entire class of
production bugs. Tool-use quality is bounded by the quality of your tool definitions.
Treating the model as deterministic is the most common mistake in agent
projects.
KEY FRAMEWORK
How tool-using LLMs are made
Pre-training — language, reasoning, world facts
Instruction tuning — act like an assistant
Tool-use training — know when to call a tool
Alignment (RLHF) — reward accurate, safe tool use
YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO
Describe the training stages behind tool-using LLMs
Balance cost, latency, and quality when choosing a
model
Build a held-out evaluation set before switching
models
Write tool schemas using the production schema
patterns
ENTERPRISE LENS · ADDISON BOYER
Before any model swap, run a held-out set of 30–100 realistic inputs — happy paths, edge cases, and failures you
already know from production.
Track input/output tokens, cache behavior, step count, and retries per run. Always check current provider pricing
before go-live.
Good candidates for a cheaper model are tasks that have run stably in production for months. Guard them with a
tight evaluation suite.
DISCUSS
→ What must a caller know from a tool error to act safely?
→ What can you reliably cause the model to do — and what can't you?
Concepts after Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 5–6. Case framing, synthesis, and enterprise lens: Addison Boyer.
